group: PSI Score: Pneumonia Severity Index for CAP
question:
Patient note:
A 68-year-old woman who lives alone in a ground-floor condominium and manages her own grocery shopping, medications, and finances came to the emergency department this morning after awakening with a deep, productive cough and low‐grade chills that began two days ago but intensified overnight. She drove herself, choosing not to stop for over-the-counter antipyretics or inhaler use because her primary-care physician had once advised her to let the hospital team see “unmasked numbers.” Her medical record lists a reduced-ejection-fraction cardiomyopathy diagnosed seven years ago after an anterior myocardial infarction; her most recent outpatient echocardiogram four months earlier documented a left-ventricular ejection fraction of 35 % with mild eccentric remodeling, for which she takes carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily and low-dose torsemide most mornings. She is also followed in a specialty clinic for compensated hepatic fibrosis related to remote hepatitis C infection; albumin and INR have remained within reference limits, and she has never developed ascites or encephalopathy. She denies any prior dialysis, nephrolithiasis, or episodes of acute kidney injury, and her last basic metabolic panel six weeks ago showed a creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL. No history of stroke, seizures, malignancy, chronic lung disease, or residence in any assisted-living facility is documented, and she remains physically active by walking her dog around the neighborhood lake each evening. She quit smoking 20 years ago after a 10-pack-year exposure, drinks a single glass of red wine on holidays, and has never used illicit substances. Vaccination records on the state registry confirm receipt of an inactivated influenza injection in October and both pneumococcal series during a cardiology admission three years ago. On arrival she sat upright on the gurney, answered questions coherently, and correctly supplied the date, location, and the names of both adult children. Skin was warm and lightly diaphoretic; capillary refill was brisk. Untreated triage vital signs obtained while breathing ambient air at this sea-level facility were: oral temperature 38.15 °C, regular radial pulse 79 beats per minute verified on a three-lead rhythm strip as sinus rhythm without ectopy, automated blood pressure 96/58 mm Hg confirmed by manual cuff, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute with moderate depth, and fingertip pulse oximetry fluctuating between 92 % and 93 %. Neck veins were not distended above the sternal angle while she reclined at 45°, and there was only trace pedal edema unchanged from cardiology clinic documentation. Cardiac auscultation revealed a crisp S1 and S2 with a soft third sound already noted on prior exams, no new murmurs, rubs, or gallops. The lung examination disclosed bronchial breath sounds and coarse crackles over the right lower posterior field along with faint late-inspiratory rales at the right mid-scapular line; percussion remained resonant throughout, and there was no dull, stony note suggestive of free fluid. The abdomen was flat and nontender with a smooth liver edge palpable 1 cm below the costal margin; no splenomegaly or shifting dullness was appreciated. A focused neurologic screen showed equal, reactive pupils, intact extra-ocular movements, fluent speech, and 5/5 strength in all extremities. Bedside glucometer prior to intravenous access read 118 mg/dL. Peripheral venipuncture and a right radial arterial stick were performed within ten minutes of bay entry, and only the minimal heparinized saline needed to keep the arterial catheter patent was used thereafter. Basic metabolic panel returned sodium 143 mEq/L, potassium 4.1 mEq/L, chloride 104 mEq/L, bicarbonate 25 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 10 mg/dL, and creatinine 0.9 mg/dL. Complete blood count showed leukocytes 12.7 × 10⁹/L with 85 % segmented neutrophils, hematocrit 38 %, hemoglobin 12.6 g/dL, and platelet count 210 × 10⁹/L. The arterial blood gas drawn on room air revealed pH 7.46, PaCO₂ 35 mm Hg, PaO₂ 88 mm Hg, calculated bicarbonate 24 mEq/L, and an A–a gradient mildly elevated for her age, consistent with early hypoxemic respiratory compromise without acid–base derangement. Serum lactate measured 1.4 mmol/L, and high-sensitivity troponin fell below assay detection limits. A portable postero-anterior chest radiograph obtained fifteen minutes into the encounter—before any antibiotics, diuretics, or supplemental oxygen—demonstrated a dense consolidation occupying the posterior segment of the right lower lobe with air bronchograms; both costophrenic angles appeared sharp, and no layering opacity or meniscus was visualized. Heart size matched prior outpatient films. Twelve-lead electrocardiography displayed sinus rhythm at 78 beats per minute with Q waves in leads V1–V3 and nonspecific T-wave flattening identical to a tracing six months earlier. Two sets of peripheral blood cultures, a spontaneously expectorated sputum sample for Gram stain and culture, urinary antigens for Streptococcus pneumoniae and Legionella pneumophila, and a multiplex respiratory viral PCR panel were dispatched to the laboratory before any antimicrobial or supportive therapy. Up to the moment this narrative is filed she has received no intravenous crystalloids, bronchodilators, vasopressors, corticosteroids, diuretics, antipyretics, or supplemental oxygen, ensuring that all physiologic observations, laboratory values, and imaging findings above represent her untreated presentation.

Question: What is the patient's Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) adds demographic, comorbidity, examination, laboratory, and radiographic points at presentation.
- Demographics: for a woman, use age minus 10: 68 − 10 = 58. She lives independently, so nursing-home residence adds 0.
- Comorbidities: chronic liver disease from hepatitis C with hepatic fibrosis = 20; heart failure with LVEF 35% = 10. No malignancy, cerebrovascular disease, or renal disease = 0.
- Examination: alert; respiratory rate 20 (<30/min), systolic BP 96 (not <90 mmHg), temperature 38.15 °C (neither <35 nor ≥40), and pulse 79 (<125/min). Each adds 0.
- Labs: pH 7.46 (not <7.35), BUN 10 (<30 mg/dL), sodium 143 (not <130 mEq/L), glucose 118 (<250 mg/dL), and hematocrit 38% (not <30%). Each adds 0. Room-air PaO₂ 88 mmHg and saturation 92–93% do not meet the hypoxemia threshold (PaO₂ <60 or saturation <90%): 0.
- Imaging: consolidation without pleural effusion = 0.
Sum: 58 + 20 + 10 + 0 = 88 (risk class III).
Final answer: 88
